requirements.text: WHEN a rendered markdown document contains an inline-code span whose entire content is a .md document reference, the system shall render that span as a clickable link to the referenced document.
WHEN the user clicks a converted inline-code .md reference, the system shall navigate to the referenced document via client-side routing without a full page reload.
IF a converted inline-code reference targets a document that does not exist in the project, THEN the system shall visibly flag the reference as broken rather than rendering a silently dead link.
IF a converted inline-code reference target escapes project boundaries or contains path traversal, THEN the system shall block navigation and flag the reference.
WHILE a .md path appears inside a fenced code block, the system shall render it verbatim without converting it to a link.
WHILE an inline-code span's content is not solely a .md document reference (genuine code, command, or example), the system shall render it verbatim without converting it to a link.
The system shall preserve existing markdown-link rendering and ticket-key linkification behavior unchanged when inline-code conversion is active.

Conversion applies only when the entire inline-code span content (after stripping an optional #anchor fragment) matches the .md document-reference shape accepted for plain-text references; spans merely containing a .md path do not convert.
Anchor fragments (#section) on converted references are supported through the existing MDT-150 URL scheme and are carried into the resolved URL.
Same-name disambiguation follows the existing MDT-150 resolution semantics (ticket-context vs documents-view mode); no new disambiguation rules are introduced.
Paths with spaces or URL-encoded characters resolve through the existing query-parameter document URL scheme (encodeURIComponent).
Documents containing many inline-code spans shall render without perceptible regression relative to current rendering (no additional network requests per span at render time).
WHILE an inline-code span names a .md file as part of a command or example sentence, the system shall apply the whole-span rule and convert only spans that are solely a reference.

WHEN an inline-code .md reference names a file that exists at the project root (e.g. src/THEME.md) while its source-relative interpretation would miss, the system shall resolve the reference to the existing project document instead of a dead relative target.

Only .md references are processed by link normalization; non-.md hrefs pass through as valid file links and are never flagged broken for their file extension. Traversal and configured-path security boundaries are unchanged.

WHEN an inline-code document reference is a bare filename whose relative interpretation is unverifiable and exactly one project file carries that basename, the system shall resolve the reference to that unique file; ambiguous or unmatched names keep the relative resolution.

Inline-code .html references are processed exactly like .md references (qualification, fallback chain, basename disambiguation, documents-route rendering); the basename map is built once per document-index load with no additional network requests.
A code span containing a full http(s) URL links the whole span to that URL (code-styled, navigable); URL-less command spans with .md words stay verbatim regardless of index state.

Link configuration is owner-level and file-level only: CONFIG_DIR/config.toml [links] (read via /api/config/global, merged over built-in defaults). The browser localStorage override and its Board-tab toggle were removed; a stale legacy key is ignored.

WHEN a plain-text path token ending in a ticket-key-shaped .md basename (e.g. docs/uat/GPDE-003.md) appears in a ticket-context document and the document index is loaded, the system shall render the whole token as ONE document link — navigable when the path exists, visibly flagged broken when the index knows it is missing — instead of splitting it into a plain path prefix plus a bare ticket link; an unknown index (null) and ..-prefixed, tickets-area, or disabled-flag tokens keep the legacy rendering byte-identically.

WHEN a link or token in a rendered document resolves into the tickets area (e.g. ../.tickets/GPDE-012-slug.md from a documents-view source, or another ticket's subdoc directory resolved from a ticket body), THEN the system shall route it to the ticket it names — the ticket view for a ticket-key .md basename, that ticket's subdoc view for a <KEY>/<rest>.md|.html path — and a bare ticket-key-shaped .md basename in documents-view mode shall route to the ticket mirroring ticket-context semantics; non-ticket-shaped targets keep their existing documents-view routing unchanged.

WHEN SmartLink evaluates a document link against the document index, THEN it shall flag the target broken only when the index positively covers the target's directory (coversPrefix) and the file is absent; targets under prefixes the index never lists (the tickets area, unconfigured directories) are unknown — rendered as normal links, never flagged broken.

scenarios.title: convert_inline_code_doc_reference
scenarios.given: Given a project containing a ticket whose body includes an inline-code reference to an existing .md document
scenarios.when: When I open that ticket in the board
scenarios.then: Then the inline-code reference renders as a clickable link

scenarios.title: client_side_navigation_no_reload
scenarios.then: Then the app navigates to the referenced document without a full page reload

scenarios.title: broken_reference_visibly_flagged
scenarios.given: Given a ticket body with an inline-code reference to a .md document that does not exist in the project
scenarios.then: Then the reference is visibly flagged as broken instead of appearing as a normal working link

scenarios.title: fenced_code_path_stays_plain
scenarios.given: Given a document containing a fenced code block that includes a .md path
scenarios.then: Then the path inside the code block renders as plain code with no link

scenarios.title: genuine_inline_code_stays_plain
scenarios.given: Given a document containing an inline-code span that is a command or example rather than solely a .md reference
scenarios.then: Then that span renders as plain inline code with no link

obligations.title: Conversion of qualifying inline-code spans must go through resolveDocumentRef and the link-placeholder mechanism, never a second conversion pass (D2/D3, covers BR-1.1)
Missing ctx or disabled enableDocumentLinks must keep protectInlineCode byte-identical to current output (D4, covers BR-3.2, BR-4.1)
Existence cache must dedupe to one in-flight fetch per project and expose sync lookup plus subscription (D5, covers BR-2.1, C5)
SmartLink broken styling for known-missing DOCUMENT targets must reuse the existing broken span rendering; unknown index renders normal link (D5/D7)
No new traversal/scope code; converted links must pass unchanged through classifyAndNormalizeLink (D6, covers BR-2.2)
Unit + e2e suites must cover conversion, preservation, anchor, encoding, traversal and existence cases

Step 1.5 ticket-filename protection captures the WHOLE path token; restore-time routing produces a documents-route link whenever the index is loaded for a path outside the tickets area with document links enabled — existing targets navigate, known-missing targets render flagged-broken via SmartLink (BR-2.1); unknown index (null), no oracle, ..-prefixed, tickets-area, and disabled flags keep the legacy split rendering byte-identically (covers BR-2.6)

resolveDocumentRef classifies tickets-area targets as ticket documents in every source mode (documents-view explicit links and bare ticket-key basenames, ticket-context other-ticket subdocs), the documents view forwards the project's configured ticketsPath into preprocessing, and SmartLink broken flagging is coverage-bounded by the document index (coversPrefix) so targets outside covered prefixes are unknown, not missing (covers BR-2.7, BR-2.8)

testPlans.title: MDT-237 Playwright: conversion render, no-reload navigation, fenced/plain preservation, broken flagging (BDD scenarios)
Existing suites must stay green: bun run fe:test and lint:frontend (BR-4.1 preservation)
MDT-237 preprocessor: genuine code, fenced code, no-context, disabled-flags, and traversal-shaped spans stay safe/verbatim; existing links unaffected
Project-root fallback resolution: absolute-exists wins, explicit .. refs never re-anchored, unknown index keeps path math
E2E: project-root fallback scenario renders documents-route link for root-existing refs from ticket subdocs
Config merge verified via inspection + e2e: getLinkConfig merges localStorage > config.toml [links] > defaults (covered by green suites run with config.toml links present; see UAT notes)
Non-.md passthrough: badge.css/unknown extensions stay valid file links; .md still processed; traversal still broken (MDT-150 normalizer amendment)
Basename disambiguation (unique wins, ambiguous keeps relative) and .html processing parity; e2e bare-filename scenario
MDT-237 preprocessor: qualifying inline-code .md spans convert to resolved links (bare, anchor, ../); nested ticket-key guard; URL-span linking; plain-text positive-knowledge routing

Plain-text path tokens with ticket-key basenames: positive-index whole-link routing, anchor/encoding, and byte-identical legacy fallback (missing/unknown oracle, disabled flags, tickets-area, ..-prefixed, bare/suffixed regression)

Tickets-area targets route to the ticket: documents-view explicit links (live GPDE-012 case), anchors, subdoc paths, bare ticket-key basenames, ticket-context other-ticket subdocs; non-ticket targets keep documents routing

SmartLink coverage-bounded flagging: tickets-area and unconfigured-prefix targets render normal links; covered-and-missing still flags (BR-2.1 preserved); unknown index stays no-signal; plus coversPrefix cache semantics
MDT-237 existence cache: null-while-loading, membership, per-project scope, subscription semantics, coversPrefix coverage bounds
Documents-view wiring: MarkdownViewer fetches the project config and forwards the configured ticketsPath to MarkdownContent; config failure falls back to the docs/CRs default
